That is an access token. It expires in $minutes minutes. Paste the refresh token, or use a fixed key in Headers.
Stays down until ${policy.recoveryThreshold} checks pass in a row, so a host that flaps does not page, clear and page again.
Re-checks every ${QuickRetry.GAP_MS / 1000}s after a failure, so it alerts about ${quickRetryLead(retries)} after the first failed check
Deleting “${monitor.displayName}” takes its history and its scheduled checks with it. There is an undo for a few seconds afterwards, and then it is gone.
The ${config.theme.label.lowercase()} preset is a fixed surface with known contrast. Choose Custom above to set your own background, text colour and transparency.
Using the ${viewModel.proxiedTimeoutSeconds}s default from Settings. A circuit to a hidden service takes far longer to build than a clearnet request takes to answer.
Re-checks every ${QuickRetry.GAP_MS / 1000}s once it answers again, so the all-clear comes about ${quickRetryLead(policy.recoveryThreshold - 1)} after the first good check
Last internal error: ${health.lastSignature}. This is a fault in Nightbell, not in the sites you are watching — their status is unchanged. It clears as soon as one check completes.
Up when every reply comes back. Degraded when some are lost, down when all ${draft.network.packets} are. They go out one second apart, and each waits for its reply up to the timeout.
Blank uses the shared ${shared.host}:${shared.port} from Settings. Fill these in only to send this monitor somewhere else, which is what watching a Tor service and an I2P one at the same time takes.

This sign-in belongs to the browser session it came from. Signing out there, or that session ending$until, signs Nightbell out. If the provider rotates tokens, Nightbell's first refresh also ends the browser's copy.
